These tables have been generated based on deidentified survey microdata.
They follow the **structure** of the originals. They have the same
forms, columns (mostly), and keys. They can be joined between forms and
across years.

## What is here

| Folder   | Form                                            | Tables |       Rows |
|-------------|---------------------------------|------------:|------------:|
| `1t_god` | 1-Т annual, enterprise labor                    |      4 | 30,025,899 |
| `1t_kv`  | 1-Т quarterly                                   |     16 | 24,480,242 |
| `d004`   | Household budget, quarterly (12 tables/quarter) |    192 |  8,612,484 |
| `2t`     | 2-Т, pay                                        |      4 |  7,328,814 |
| `t001`   | Т-001, labor force                              |      4 |  1,885,110 |
| `d008`   | Household roster (persons)                      |      4 |    169,059 |
| `d002`   | Subject & assessment                            |      8 |     95,542 |
| `d006`   | Dwelling                                        |      4 |     46,743 |

One `.csv` per original table (UTF-8), laid out as
`<form>/<year>/[<quarter>/]<table>.csv` — the same shape and the same
file names as the source. `MANIFEST.csv` lists every table with its
synthetic and real row and column counts.

## How the tables join

**`NOMER` is the household key** and it works exactly as in the real
data. Within a year it links the roster (`d008`), the dwelling (`d006`),
the attitudes tables (`d002`) and all 48 quarterly budget tables
(`d004`). A person is `NOMER` + `NOMP`.

These joins hold *by construction.* The households are generated once as
a backbone and then every form is drawn from it. In the shipped tables,
every `d006` row resolves to a household and `TE`/`K` agree with the
roster for 100% of them.

**`ID` is the enterprise key** in 1-Т and 2-Т. Synthetic ids look like
`S-2t-2023-000001`; real ids are all digits, so no synthetic id can
collide with a real one.

**The same household and the same enterprise recur across years**, so
over-time analysis is possible.

## Reading the values

Almost every field is a numeric *code*, as in the source — `POL` is sex,
but whether `1` is male is not documented for most forms. Value
codebooks exist for most of the forms and sit in the `documentation`
folder. I suggest that you carve out some time to examine those
codebooks.

Open the files with any tool that reads CSV. Do not open the large ones
in Excel: several tables exceed its 1,048,576-row limit and it will
silently truncate them.

## The original documentation

The folder `documentation/` holds the material that shipped inside the
source archives, organised by form and year: **36** table-structure
documents, **45** reference books and code lists, **15** blank
questionnaires and **3** interviewer instructions.
`documentation/INDEX.csv` lists them all with what each one is.

These describe the forms, not any respondent, and they are the authority
on what a column means. Note that the same filename can hold different
content in different years, which is why the folder keeps the year
structure.

## Limitations

> A few words on the difference between synthetic and real data.

| Limitation | Measured |
|----------------------------------------------------|--------------------|
| Sythesis shrinks standard errors a little. | — |
| Associations *between* variables are roughly halved.  Signs are right in almost all the cases, but the effect size also shrinks. You may treat coefficient estimates as lower bounds for real effects. | dwelling area on household size 0.100 vs 0.171 |
| Year-to-year persistence in the 1-Т panel is about half the real value | 0.49 / 0.24 vs 0.93 / 0.79 |
| Row counts differ slightly: coverage and rows-per-unit are modelled, not copied | median +0.13% / −0.23% |
| Т-001 have been generated on 40 out of the original 154 columns. Most of those columns had more than 90% of missing values anyways. | — |
| In 2021 the respondent's age is not tied to the person named — that year's roster has no birth year at all | — |
| D-004's `kv_vopr1` repeats items within a household more than the real data does | 15% of rows vs 2.4% |
